outlook: Grains were mixed in overnight trade Thursday after Wednesday's broad selloff. December corn edged up about a penny to $5.03 after testing support near $5.00, while November soybeans slipped 3 cents to $12.95 and Minneapolis December spring wheat was nearly unchanged at $7.10; December Chicago wheat recovered 2.5 cents to $6.89 as Taiwan and Jordan sought milling wheat. A strong U.S. dollar and the highest long-term Treasury yields in nearly 25 years weighed on the commodity complex Wednesday, and traders are positioning ahead of Friday's USDA WASDE and Crop Production reports, where analysts expect corn yield near 177.7 bu/acre versus 178.5 in September. ICE November canola bounced C$13.10 to C$823.40 after Wednesday's drop; Minneapolis cash bids shown are from Wednesday's USDA report.
